newsitem.title: HONG KONG: "I'll keep British knighthood" - Tung's HK advisor.
newsitem.headline: "I'll keep British knighthood" - Tung's HK advisor.

text.p: The senior advisor to Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Monday he had no plans to jettison his knighthood awarded for serving under four consecutive British Governors.
"I will not give up my British honours," Chung Sze-yuen told a news conference.

He said the knighthood was awarded for his services to the people of Hong Kong but he did not expect the post-colonial government to recognise it just as the present British colonial administration did not recognise his Order of Sacred Treaure awarded by Japan.

Chung, 79, retired from public service in 1988 as a senior Executive Councillor -- the British Governor's inner cabinet of advisers -- but agreed to come out of retirement to perform the same function for Tung in the delicate period following the handover of Hong Kong to China on June 30.
